output.name: Sóleth
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up and away, and the wind had nothing to carry it home. But wind is still wind, and Tavo the Gale was in a good mood that year. Ennu sewed a white kite for a girl of the Gannet Rocks, who was to marry a boy who kept goats on the far side of the sound. Her mother tied the tail long, so the kite would drag its ribbons down the cliff to the new door. Tavo lifted it, and Tavo tore at it, and then Tavo laughed and set it down gently on the roof. The Gulls saw this and carried the story up to Vel. Hesk counted the knots in the tail and said the count was good. So when you see the white kite in the north, do not call it lost. It is a bride's kite, still tied to the house it was meant for, and the wind is still blessing that door. Mind your own knots, and tell the girl to tie her tail long.
output.verse:
White cloth on the cord,
its tail trails down to her door,
blown home, the bride is wed.
